summary: Every valid result contains all C(n,k) combinations explicitly, so output construction itself matches the required bound. A direct output lower bound and the pruned search upper bound certify the current solution more precisely than runtime scaling.

optimality.argument: The result contains C(n,k) distinct lists of length k, requiring Omega(k * C(n,k)) values to be written. The current search follows exactly one increasing path per combination, prunes prefixes that cannot reach length k, and copies exactly k values at each leaf, giving O(k * C(n,k)) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Any valid return value explicitly materializes C(n,k) combinations, and each combination contains k integers, so the output alone has k * C(n,k) elements.
Strictly increasing choices give each combination one leaf, the loop bound rejects every prefix without enough remaining values, and each emitted path copy costs O(k).
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover multiple combinations and the single-value domain; black-box real-test execution passed all five existing ordinary correctness checks.
